thread.title: You might be paying for iPhone app subscriptions you're not using — here's how to cancel them (AAPL)

author: sfgate.com
title: You might be paying for iPhone app subscriptions you're not using — here's how to cancel them (AAPL)
text:
Justin Sullivan/Getty Images
You might have several monthly or annual subscriptions for content or apps billed through iTunes. Here's how you can check what you're subscribed to through Apple. Nobody likes paying for things they don't use.
 MoviePass 'Un-Canceling' Users' Accounts The once unlimited movie subscription service recently updated their plans. Starting August 15, users were shifted to a new plan limiting them to just three movies per month for $9.95. Many customers canceled their service following the announcement. Most subscribers assumed they would be able to use their service for the remainder of the month they already paid for. But some users may have reactivated their account without even knowing it. An opt-in page popped up for both active and inactive members to inform them of the recent changes. If you tapped the “More Details” link and tapped “I Accept”, you reactivated your account. How do you avoid reactivating your account? 1. When presented with the opt-in screen, tap the X in the upper right-hand corner. 2. Don’t use your MoviePass for the remainder of your subscription. 3. Double check your status and be sure you have officially canceled your service.
Media: Wibbitz So if you're an iPhone user, you should double-check to make sure you didn't accidentally stay subscribed to an app or service you thought you cancelled.
It's actually pretty hidden in the App Store — TechCrunch's Josh Constine called the settings "buried" and a "dark pattern design."
App subscriptions are an emphasis for Apple. It held an invite-only meeting last year to convince developers to adopt subscription models, and Apple CEO Tim Cook said that 300 million Apple users are currently subscribed to either an app or an Apple subscription service, like Apple Music.
Here's how you check your subscriptions . You can tap here if you have the iTunes store installed on your iPhone or Mac.
Otherwise, you'll have to fire up the App Store app. You're looking for your photo in the corner:
Business Insider
That will take you to this page. Again, you'll want to tap on your user photo.
Business Insider
After tapping on your account again, you'll need to enter your password, scan your fingerprint, or use Face ID to get to the next page. You're looking for "Subscriptions," which should be on the lower half of your screen:
Business Insider
That will bring you to the subscriptions screen. Tapping anything on this list will tell you how much you're spending, when it renews next, and the opportunity to cancel or change the settings.
Business Insider
Here's what the subscription screen for Apple Music looks like:
Business Insider
There are more details and options at Apple's website, but you'll be able to similarly cancel your unwanted subscriptions.
